text:
deploy-bot: scheduling maintenance slot 03:00 UTC 2026-05-02 for migration `email_index_backfill_v1`. Plan: add sparse index for `emails.normalized` and run a safe backfill in non-blocking batches. Canary: index build + backfill on db-shard-3, 10m observation.

emma: ack. quick summary of risk: index build should be CONCURRENTLY, backfill updates ~5M rows if predicate misses. We avoid table locks but still watch bloat/replica lag.

ryan: rollback owner here. triggers: (a) write error rate > 0.8% for 5m, (b) replica lag > 12s sustained, (c) lock wait p99 > 250ms for 2 minutes. If triggered -> pause backfill, drop new index if needed, revert service pin.

lucy: version pin note: pin web-api to 3.2.0 for the window. This contains the new query plan that uses the sparse index; older versions may not use index and increase load.

dave: runbook and SQL in runbook doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/email_index_backfill_v1 

Snippet (backfill controller):
```
-- safe chunked update
WITH c AS (
  SELECT id FROM emails WHERE normalized IS NULL LIMIT 1000 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
)
UPDATE emails e
SET normalized = lower(trim(e.body))
FROM c
WHERE e.id = c.id;
```

opsbot: slot reserved by @emma. reminder 02:40 UTC preflight.

emma: preflight checklist: replicas caught up (<5s), monitor alert on, pg_stat_activity no long tx > 30s, canary runbook tab ready. I posted checklist to /docs/releases/email_index_backfill/checklist.md

deploy-bot: canary started: shard=3, index create CONCURRENTLY initiated. logs -> /logs/deploy/1763619999/canary-3

ryan: 5m canary update: index create progressing, no blocking locks. backfill started on shard-3 controller PID 8921. rows/sec ~420. no errors so far. bumping to canary traffic 15%.

lucy: monitoring query: explain plans look good. watch replica lag and sequential scan counts. Dashboard: /dashboards/eng/releases/email_index_backfill_v1

emma: added alert: email_index_backfill_high_lag -> page #eng-oncall if replica lag > 12s for 3m.

dave: note: if we must abort, we run `pg_cancel_backend` on controller and run `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY if_exists emails_normalized_idx;` then unpin service. Kill controllers gracefully.

opsbot: alert rule created. paging configured.

ryan: canary 20m mark: slight uptick in write latency p95 (~180ms -> 210ms) but within threshold. error rate flat. proceeding to 50% in waves of 25%.

emma: hold - noticing replicas in region eu-west1 show 6s lag, still OK. continuing. please keep an eye on bloat metrics.

lucy: started a small bloom filter probe to estimate index selectivity before full rollout. results look favorable (~98% selectivity).

ryan: mid-rollout check: one transient spike to 0.9% error rate correlated with a malformed batch from controller. we rolled that batch back; errors returned to baseline. not hitting rollback trigger. note to add validation to controller.

emma: can we tighten controller retry backoff? dave can you patch now?

dave: pushed small patch to controller to validate payload and backoff jitter. pin new controller image tag `email-bf-controller:20260502-1` during remainder of rollout.

deploy-bot: rolling remainder in 25% waves. current rollout 100% at 03:35 UTC. logs archived.

ryan: post-rollout actions: run `VACUUM` on affected partitions off-peak, schedule index maintenance in 24h. create PM ticket to check bloat and replication health.

emma: post-mortem notes to capture: time-to-detect faulty batch, time-to-stop backfill, index drop time if needed. Also verify no long-running transactions remained.

lucy: added release-note blurb and user-visible note about faster email lookups.

opsbot: deploy complete. thread closed. :white_check_mark:
